newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan sees risk of spiralling budget deficits.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan sees risk of spiralling budget deficits.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned again on Wednesday of the risk of U.S. budget deficits spiralling out of control in the next century if early action is not taken to stem government red ink.
"We are still in the area where that vicious circle can be cut off," he said.

In a speech to the National Association of Business Economists, the central bank chief foresaw sharply mounting outlays for Medicare and Medicaid health care for the elderly and poor as the baby boom generation starts to retire.
Greenspan zeroed in on the consumer price index (CPI), which is used to make annual cost-of-living changes in a wide range of government programs, including Social Security.
As he has done before, Greenspan argued that the CPI overstates inflation. "There is no doubt that we have got a real bias," he said.
That upward bias in the CPI bloats government benefit payments and thus the federal budget deficit.
"There is no doubt that the issue of the CPI is a very crucial question with respect to resolving the very difficult budget problem," Greenspan said.
